title: Subbing for Harrison Barnes in Chris Kelly's band
summary: Robinson filled in for welder Harrison Barnes in Chris Kelly's band, and traces where Sonny Henry played afterward.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: How many days you had steady you worked with Chris? Were you a member of Chris's band? Who me?

Who me? No, no, no. I never remember Chris's band. I always remember Chris's band like when someone played, Harrison Bourne was working over at, in the shop, moving out of here. In the shop with a well-tooled, with a bottle of tubes. And when Harrison would get off to play, he'd say, Chris come get me. And he'd tell Chris to get me, come get me, you see. And I'd go play. And Harrison was a welder, you see. He was a welder. Flu welder they call him. A man of a job like that, you know, good and well. He'd have been welding the flues all day, looking at that hot violin, that kind of stuff. That flame. When he come up there, he won't rest, you see. But many nights I'd just spend time, sometimes three and four jobs. Okay. In his place, of course, for a week. But he always, he'd work him, at Friday, and Saturdays. Sometime he'd work Sunday, sometime I'd work, if I don't have nothing to do, I'd work Sunday in his place, Sunday night. In other words, if he'd work Sunday night, he'd work the job around about 11 o'clock, you see. Because he lived up in the house here, you see. And I'd go to the fancy job up, you see. Fancy's job up.
Let's see, I thought Sonny played with Chris for a while.

Yeah, Sonny played with Chris for a while. Yeah, Sonny played with Chris for a while. Good while, too. Sonny went with, with, uh, at the Lick with, lived with, uh, Emmis White. Went to Lick, the half-road house, they call it. Wrecked with Emmis White. What kind of house? Eh?

The half-road house, at the Lick. Oh. And he went there on a, but a year and something, Emmis White. So I closed down, well, Emmis went on to St. Louis, Missouri. Then Sonny went to White with Chris a little while, after that. Then, then after that, Sonny went with Hitler and Charles. And Charles went with Louis Demain. And Louis Demain, he went up on a music box. Well, Crownlip and Cunhael. Worked there, but three or four, three or four years, music box. The only things, it's a lot of things, man, you know, you forget, you know. Yeah. You forget.
